title: Skin Lesions
portrait_note: N'Gavu — young Black man, mustard-yellow party jacket likeness, thin mustache, tired bloodshot eyes; hospital gown on ED stretcher; blistered dorsal hands and forearms, fragile skin; mustard-yellow shirt draped on bedside chair; two brown beer bottles on overbed side table (patient property); MeWorld sculptural CGI clinical still

rationale.Urine porphyrins: Porphyrins keep building in the skin until you measure them — elevated uroporphyrins confirm the photosensitive pathway.
rationale.Plasma porphyrins: Circulating porphyrin peak at 620 nm locks the diagnosis when urine is equivocal.
rationale.HCV / HIV / Iron studies: Acquired PCT is often triggered by alcohol, iron overload, or silent hepatitis — the rash is not the whole story.
rationale.Phlebotomy: First-line when iron overload is driving the process — target ferritin low-normal.
rationale.Sun protection / Avoid alcohol: Sunlight activates porphyrins in skin; alcohol keeps the trigger running — both must stop.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a man from our village who came to the ED after a weekend of drinking with friends. He was partying — beer all night — and thought nothing of it until the next afternoon, walking home in the sun, when his skin began to peel and blister on his hands, face, and forearms. Light through the window still hurts. He took off his yellow party shirt when they put him in a gown; it hangs by the bedside. His beer bottles sit on the side table — his property, he says. On exam: fragile bullae and erosions on sun-exposed skin, milia, hyperpigmentation, and hypertrichosis on the dorsal hands. PCT is the most common porphyria — uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency leads to uroporphyrin accumulation in skin and photosensitivity. Acquired triggers: alcohol, hepatitis C, HIV, hemochromatosis, estrogen. Diagnosis: elevated urine porphyrins, plasma porphyrin peak at 620 nm. Treatment: phlebotomy for iron overload, sun avoidance, stop alcohol, screen HCV/HIV/iron.
